solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Penny each for this vegetable?

parts.note: penny abbreviates to P and each to EA, so the vegetable's name is literally those two abbreviations with a split before them

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether some vegetable is priced at a penny apiece.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: SPLIT, then P (penny) and EA (each), the abbreviations of the two clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried peas halved along their natural seam are a common pulse sold for soups.

clue.text: Job cabby will do for a score

definitions.meaning: a taxi driver's job is collecting a fare from the kerb
to score is slang for obtaining something

explanation.surface: A taxi driver says what work he will take on for twenty pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a score' tempts as twenty; 'for' is the link and 'score' the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab collecting a passenger, and slang for an acquisition, are both this hyphenated noun.

clue.text: I found his howl disruptive, screening the entrance of Ronnie Barker

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind or around, so the jumbled words enclose the next piece
something disruptive throws things into disorder, so the words I found his howl are jumbled
the entrance of a word is its first letter, taken from Ronnie

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a howl ruining their viewing of the comedian Ronnie Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Barker was a British comedian; the clue splits his name so 'Barker' alone is the definition, a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A barker is a whimsical word for a dog, and this huge hound is a breed of one.

clue.text: Go with current SA president cutting spicy food

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the president's name goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: go, as in energy or vim, means pep
I is the physics symbol for electric current
Juan Peron was president of Argentina in South America

explanation.surface: A rallying call to back a South American leader who is slashing hot dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is South America here, not South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a heavily seasoned dried sausage, widely used as a pizza topping.

clue.text: This with tip of tongue animates doctors

definitions.text: This with tip of tongue animates doctors

indicators.note: doctors as a verb means tampers with, so the letters of animates are rearranged
the tip of a word is its first letter, here from tongue

explanation.surface: A condition that, with something on the tip of the tongue, brings medics to life.
explanation.walkthrough: Add the T from 'tip of tongue' to the answer and the letters rearrange into ANIMATES; 'tip of the tongue' is also the feeling of a word you cannot recall.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory loss is just what leaves a word stuck on the tip of the tongue, and doctors study it.

clue.text: Winehouse well-stacked, which produces crime

parts.note: well-stacked is slang for large or buxom
Amy Winehouse was a British singer

explanation.surface: A tabloid remark about the singer Winehouse's figure somehow leads to an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winehouse' is the singer Amy Winehouse; the descriptive word comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already wed is an offence in many legal systems.

clue.text: Extra billion paid for by Obama?

parts.note: if a meal is on someone, they are paying for it
Barack Obama stood for the United States as its president

explanation.surface: An extra billion in spending, funded by the American president?
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid for by' gives ON, as in 'drinks are on me'; Obama stands for the US he led.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment over and above the usual is an additional reward.

clue.text: Pass on, or fail on seance?

definitions.meaning: to pass on is a euphemism for to die
a medium who fails at a seance would surrender, not produce, a spirit

explanation.surface: Two meanings: dying, or a medium's flop at a spiritualist sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is read literally: a failed seance gives up (fails to deliver) the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for dying, or for a machine finally ceasing to work, read literally of a spirit.

clue.text: The province of Homo sapiens one needs in full, TBA

parts.note: Homo sapiens is mankind, man
one as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: written in full, the first word of the abbreviation is spelt out completely

explanation.surface: Mankind's domain needs, in full, something to be announced.
explanation.walkthrough: TBA stands for 'to be announced'; spelling out its first word gives TO BA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the prairie provinces of Canada.

clue.text: Fight? I'm in for a stint

indicators.note: in for means standing in place of, so these letters replace the letter a

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone spoiling for a fight says they are up for a spell of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stint' is a verb here, meaning to be sparing, not a spell of work.
explanation.definitionFit: To stint is to be frugal or skimp on spending, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Zip opening? It doesn't do itself justice, as it happens

definitions.text: It doesn't do itself justice, as it happens

parts.note: zip is slang for nothing
a vent is an opening or aperture

explanation.surface: A zip fastener that sticks when opened, failing to live up to its promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip opening' looks like a fly being undone; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion that is a disappointing anticlimax falls short of its billing when it takes place.

clue.text: Hard-hearted as the OT with 38 books?

definitions.meaning: the Old Testament has 39 books, so with 38 it lacks one, the Book of Ruth

explanation.surface: Asks whether a cruel person resembles a short-changed Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the Book of Ruth from the 39-book Old Testament and it is literally without Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: Merciless and pitiless are standard synonyms for showing no compassion.

clue.text: If shut, new butcher's required

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of if shut form a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: If the old butcher's shop closes, a new one will be needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher's' is rhyming slang: butcher's hook = look, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a quick look or glance.

clue.text: Game is how I won notable material

definitions.text: Game is how I won notable material

indicators.note: game means willing to try anything, so the letters of the words that follow are up for rearranging

explanation.surface: A winner boasts that their game strategy earned them memorable stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is the anagram signal; the remaining words, all of them, rearrange into the title of the TV quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous television quiz show is the anagram's result, and the whole clue reads as a contestant's boast.

clue.text: See 3
So-and-so's pasty, initially short on filling?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so this piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: a thin sandwich or pie is skimpy on its filling
pasty here means like paste, sticky or gluey

explanation.surface: Someone's Cornish pasty, at first, is skimpy on its filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the pie but is an adjective, paste-like; 'initially' puts the skimpy word first.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for someone or something whose name escapes you, like what's-his-name.

clue.text: Unfit to play the childcatcher?

parts.note: the word splits into child, a mischievous imp, and catcher, one who lassoes
a catcher with a lasso is a roper

explanation.surface: Someone is deemed unsuitable to act the Child Catcher villain on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The Child Catcher is the villain of the film Chitty Chitty Bang Bang; read as child-catcher it gives IMP plus ROPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorous or unsuitable conduct is unfit for the occasion.

clue.text: See 13
One's suggested egg in one's order

indicators.note: in signals the explosive goes inside the rearranged letters
order means arrangement, so the letters of one are put in a new sequence

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter
egg is old military slang for a bomb or mine

explanation.surface: Someone suggests an egg dish as their choice when ordering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is old slang for an explosive device, a mine; 'One's suggested' means one who is put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate put forward for a post or award has been proposed by someone.

clue.text: Mate's wearing setter's ace jumper — it's astonishing!

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so one piece is clothed in the other

parts.note: setter's means the setter is, I'm
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a pal is a mate

explanation.surface: An exclamation of amazement that a friend is wearing the crossword setter's best sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater but is the leaping African antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: This African antelope is famed for its prodigious leaps.

clue.text: Would parenthood make me dote?

indicators.note: make signals that the letters are put together anew: the answer plus dote rearranges to parenthood

explanation.surface: A child without parents wonders whether having them would make it doting.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is 'me': its letters with DOTE are the letters of PARENTHOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A child deprived of parents would long for exactly that kind of family bond.

clue.text: Seabird going wee-wee in Boulogne?

definitions.meaning: a tropical tern known for its tameness
wee-wee suggests French oui oui, the French name for Enid Blyton's toy character

explanation.surface: A seagull relieving itself in a French port town.
explanation.walkthrough: In France Enid Blyton's Noddy is called Oui-Oui; 'wee-wee' looks like toilet talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tern is named this, and so is the children's character known in France as Oui-Oui.

clue.text: Find the lady limping onto vessels

indicators.note: onto means placed after, so this piece follows the vessels

parts.note: mugs are drinking vessels
a game leg is a lame one, so game means limping

explanation.surface: Someone hobbles after cups while searching for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Find the lady is the three-card trick, a street con where the punter always loses.
explanation.definitionFit: A con no punter can win is a pointless pursuit, a fool's errand.

clue.text: See 7
Place of dubious reputation doing business, one slinging mud inside

indicators.note: inside signals that these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: a shop doing business is open
one as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: slinging means throwing about, so the letters of mud are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A shady venue is open for business while someone hurls mud indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slinging' turns MUD into UMD, which with I goes into OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunt for smoking narcotics is a disreputable establishment.

clue.text: Low note so advances money

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
in tonic sol-fa the note after soh is lah

explanation.surface: A deep note goes up the scale, bringing in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is a cow's sound; in sol-fa (do re mi fa soh lah) soh moves up to lah.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a slang word for cash, like dough or bread.

clue.text: When passport enters brawl?

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the passport's letters sit within the brawl

parts.note: a fray is a brawl or fight
a passport is a form of ID

explanation.surface: Asks at what point a travel document gets caught up in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is the definition: a day of the week answers 'when?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekday name answers the question of time, saying on which day something happens.

clue.text: Eat-in cooking houses the torture of Luxor?

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the reworked letters hold the next piece
cooking means fiddling or concocting, so the letters of eat-in are reworked

parts.note: gyp is British slang for pain, as in giving someone gyp

explanation.surface: A takeaway kitchen subjecting diners to a Luxor-style torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat-in' looks like a dining choice but is the anagram fodder; 'torture' is British slang usage, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'. Luxor is a city on the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxor lies in Egypt, so anything from there is of that nation.
